cards.title: ◐ Claude Code
cards.reviewNotes:
Your logo is now in the app and the dashboard. The background adapts to light and dark mode, and I checked it on the Home header in dark mode.

A JPEG can't change its black background, so I redrew the logo as a vector shape with a transparent background. Your original measures as about `#FA4F3B`, so I used that for the rings. The pin is white in dark mode and black in light mode, with a see-through hole. Next to your original it matches closely.

Where it appears now:
- **Home header:** replaces the old orange tile next to "E-Alert".
- **Onboarding:** first screen, shown large.
- **Dashboard:** sidebar, plus the browser-tab icon, which also switches its pin color with light/dark mode.
- **Splash screen:** two versions, black pin on a light background and white pin on a black one.
- **App icon:** your JPEG as it is, since the dark tile suits an icon.

You'll only see the new app icon and splash screen after a fresh build (`npx expo run:ios`), because Expo Go shows its own icon. The in-app logo already shows on the simulator.

The logo shape is defined once in `packages/shared/src/logo.ts`, so the app, the dashboard and the icons all draw it the same way. Typecheck, lint and the dashboard build all pass.

history.notes:
The caveman skill isn't installed, so I'll just talk caveman style myself.

Me see two things happen:

- **Academic PDF Translation plugin**: installed and working. It adds a translate skill plus batch-translator and reviewer agents.
- **`npx ccplaybooks add academic-research-skills`**: made a new `./CLAUDE.md` in the folder you ran it from, probably `/Users/jericho/E-Alert`. Every Claude session started there now follows its rules. The text comes from someone else's GitHub repo (Imbad0202/academic-research-skills), and me not read it yet.

Me can read that `CLAUDE.md` and tell you what rules it adds before you lean on it. What you want next?

history.prompt: "/var/folders/8d/4s2qjkl52md0jw6t6lyqd6k00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_o5gD7n/Screenshot 2026-11-26 at 4.36.09 PM.png"  There is a top unused space. Also, I want the cricles on the top of the sos button to be the emergency. Fire, Flood, etc.
history.notes:
I fixed both things on the Home screen and checked them on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.4). Typecheck and lint pass.

- **Top gap:** gone. The iOS tab bar already moves screens below the status bar, and my code was adding that space a second time. The same fix is applied to the Map, Navigate and list screens.
- **Emergency circles:** the row above SOS is now Medical, Fire, Police, Flood and Earthquake, and all five fit on screen. Picking one is optional:
  - **With a pick:** tap a circle and the hint changes to "Tap 3 times to send Fire alert". The triple tap goes straight to the 5-second cancel countdown with that type.
  - **Without a pick:** the "What's happening?" sheet still asks.
  - **To clear:** tap the selected circle again.
- **Flood and Earthquake** are both the thesis "Disaster" category underneath. The alert still shows the name the person picked.
- **Contacts:** they moved off Home. They're still in the small avatar row under SOS and in the Contacts tab.

The gear button over the Earthquake circle is Expo's dev menu, which only shows in development builds.

All the phase 1 screens from the plan are built with mock data: resident and responder sides of the app, plus the admin dashboard. Three things are still open:
- **Android:** no emulator on this Mac, so I haven't run it.
- **Dashboard map:** the map uses MapLibre with free OpenFreeMap tiles instead of Google Maps, because Google needs an API key. Map tiles didn't draw in my headless screenshots (no WebGL there), so check them in a real browser.
- **Not yet tested on the simulator:** the SOS flow itself and the VoiceOver / largest text size checks. I can't tap the simulator from here.

The new git repo in E-Alert has nothing committed yet.

Two servers are still running if you want to try it:
- **Mobile:** Metro on port 8081. Press Cmd+R in the simulator to reload.
- **Dashboard:** http://localhost:5199

history.prompt: "/var/folders/8d/4s2qjkl52md0jw6t6lyqd6k00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_9iXRVo/Screenshot 2026-11-26 at 10.11.11 PM.png"  "/var/folders/8d/4s2qjkl52md0jw6t6lyqd6k00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptur "/var/folders/8d/4s2qjkl52md0jw6t6lyqd6k00000gn/T/TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui_ZABWjW/Screenshot 2026-11-26 at 10.11.24 PM.png" eui_wD3NtE/Screenshot 2026-11-26 at 10.11.17 PM.png"  This is from the old UI of EALERT, i want you to proceed on adding these missing features to the current one but i want the same design as the current one /plan
history.notes:
I added all three old-app features in the new design, but I could only check one on screen (the responder Message button). You were tapping the simulator while I tested, so my deep links kept landing on whatever you had open. I stopped touching it so I don't mess up your session. Typecheck and lint pass.

- **Chat tab:** tabs are now Home · Map · Chat · Contacts · Profile.
  - **List:** search, Active and Earlier sections, a verified badge and online dot on each avatar, a category label, and an unread count. The Chat tab icon also shows an unread badge.
  - **Thread:** floating glass header with back, name and a green call button. Your bubbles are coral, the other side's are white, and system lines ("Nurse Joy accepted your alert") sit in the middle.
  - **Quick replies:** one-tap chips ("Please help ASAP!", "I'm safe now", "Need more time"…). The Send button stays grey until you type.
  - **Fake replies:** after you send, a canned reply comes back in 2.5 s so the demo feels live. It goes away when we connect Firestore in phase 2.
- **Responder tracking** (the active alert screen):
  - a glass "Your responder is on the way" banner
  - glass map buttons for zoom in/out, show whole route, and center on me
  - two tiles: "~3 min, Estimated arrival" and "0.9 km, Road distance"
  - Call and Message buttons; Message shows the unread count
  - "I'm safe now" (green) and a separate "Cancel alert" (red text, for false alarms). Both ask to confirm, and the reason is saved for the admin.
- **Map tab:** while an alert is active, the bottom card says "Help is on the way" with a Track button.
- **Responder side:** Navigate now has Backup and Message (it opens the same thread, with responder quick replies like "I'm 2 min away"). "I've arrived" moved to its own full-width row.
- **Home:** the active-alert banner shows the newest unread message from the responder.

Plain coral with white text fails accessibility contrast (3.2:1), so your own bubbles use a darker coral, `#D03E24` (4.8:1, which passes).

**Still not checked on the simulator:** the chat list, the thread, and the upgraded tracking screen. To see them:
1. Fully close Expo Go and reopen it. After switching from 4 tabs to 5, a hot reload opened the wrong tab.
2. As a resident: triple-tap SOS, then check the tracking screen and tap Message.
3. Open the Chat tab.

Light/dark and VoiceOver checks are also still open, and nothing is committed to git yet.

history.prompt: I want you to proceed on combining flood and earthquake (just make it into disaster). Then replace the ? button to be a 911 button. So 911 then the notification button.
history.notes:
Both changes are in, checked on the simulator in dark mode. Typecheck and lint pass.

- **Disaster:** Flood and Earthquake are now one "Disaster" circle with the waves icon. The row is Medical · Fire · Police · Disaster, which matches the four categories in your thesis and fits the screen without scrolling.
- **911 button:** the "?" button is gone. The header now reads 911, then the notification bell. The 911 button is a red pill with a phone icon.
  - Tapping it first asks "Call 911?", so a stray tap never dials.
  - Confirming opens the phone dialer.
  - The white-on-red text passes accessibility contrast because it is large and bold.

The "What kind of help? Optional" label and the contacts avatar stack under SOS no longer show on your screen, which looks like an edit on your side. I left them as they are.

cards.title: Run the mobile mode
cards.reviewNotes:
Mobile app running. Expo dev server up on port 8081, hot reload on.

I installed dependencies first because the workspace had none.

**Open it:**
- **Phone (Expo Go):** open `exp://192.168.18.233:8081` in Expo Go. Phone must be on same Wi-Fi as Mac. No QR code shows here because the terminal has no interactive screen.
- **Web:** http://localhost:8081
- **iOS simulator / Android:** run `! cd apps/mobile && npx expo start --ios` (or `--android`) yourself. Those need the interactive Expo menu.

Logs stream in background. Say "logs" to see output, or "stop" to kill the server.

**Your thesis is now public.** The repo is set to public, so anyone can see and download `Manuscript/E-Alert_Thesis_Revised_v4.pdf`. - **Contact circles removed** (`src/app/(resident)/home.tsx`): the small circles with initials (MD, PS, AC, RV) are gone. The line "Your SOS goes to the nearest verified responder…" is still there.

The TypeScript check found no errors in either file, but I haven't looked at it on a phone. On small screens the row may be too wide to fit, so it would scroll sideways. If that happens, I can make the buttons a little smaller.
